hero.headline: 135 kg of payload space is available on BLK3 Flight 2.
hero.subhead: Reserve capacity on an upcoming Exos Aerospace BLK3 suborbital flight, targeted for early 2027 from Spaceport America, New Mexico.
hero.positioning: Exos Aerospace has been flying since 2018 and is one of only three FAA-licensed reusable rocket launch providers in the US.

whySuborbital.title: Suborbital flight de-risks orbital programs
whySuborbital.body: A suborbital flight exposes your hardware to real launch loads, vacuum, and microgravity — then returns it to you. It is a low-cost, fast-turnaround way to validate payloads, sensors, and processes before committing to an orbital campaign. Exos positions BLK3 as a de-risk platform for orbital programs, not as an orbital launch service.
points: Flight-qualify hardware under real boost and vacuum conditions
Recover your payload after the flight for inspection and iteration
Short mission timeline and fast vehicle turnaround
Reduce program risk before scaling to an orbital mission
